questions.question: What type of application are you building?
questions.why: This fundamentally affects the technology stack, UI/UX requirements, performance constraints, and deployment strategy. A mobile app needs battery efficiency and offline capabilities; a web app needs browser compatibility; an API service needs different architecture entirely.

questions.question: What weather data and timeframe should the app provide?
questions.why: This determines data storage requirements, API choices, update frequency, and complexity. Current conditions only is simpler than multi-day forecasts with historical data. Each option requires different backend infrastructure and data sources.

options.label: All of the above plus historical data and alerts

questions.question: What is the expected scale and user type?
questions.why: This changes reliability requirements, uptime SLAs, caching strategies, and infrastructure needs. A hobby project vs. enterprise service with 1M+ users need completely different specs around performance, cost, and support.

questions.question: Should the app provide data for multiple locations or just one?
questions.why: This affects database design, search/location features, user preferences storage, and global data sourcing strategy. Supporting any location globally is more complex than a single-location or region-specific app.

questions.question: Does the app need to integrate with other services or expose APIs to developers?
questions.why: This determines whether the spec needs to include API documentation, third-party integrations, webhook support, or data export formats. Standalone apps vs. platforms serving other developers have completely different architectural requirements.

options.label: Integrate with other apps (calendar, maps, etc.)
Expose public API for third-party developers
